steps.heading: Three steps to get started
steps.step1Body: Join with the link, QR code or class code from your teacher or classmates. If your class isn’t there yet, you can create it.

features.heading: How far you’ve got. Never what you wrote.
features.body: The text of your reports and drafts stays private, even from your team.
features.barBody: How much of your report is written, or how many hours you’ve studied, at a glance. The report itself is never shared.
features.recentBody: When a teammate hasn’t logged in a while, their stamp changes color. It’s a cue to check in, not a mark against them.
features.nudgeBody: Send a short message to a teammate who seems stuck. There’s a daily limit, so nobody gets flooded.
features.docsBody: Count the characters in a Google Doc you choose, automatically. Study Pods opens only the file you pick, and never stores its text.

faq.heading: Before you start
faq.teacherQ: Can my professor see my progress?
faq.teacherA: No. Your progress is visible only to the members of your team.
faq.passwordA: No. You log in with a 6-digit code (or the button) sent to your university email.
faq.podSizeQ: How many people can be in a team?
faq.podSizeA: Up to six. Small groups make it easier to notice how everyone is doing.
faq.docsQ: What if I don’t use Google Docs?
faq.docsA: That’s fine. You can log characters written or hours studied yourself.
faq.anyClassQ: Does it work for any class?
faq.anyClassA: Yes. With an @andrew.ac.jp address, you can create or join a class for any course.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Study Pods (“the service”) is a study app built and run by a student. This page explains what the service collects, how it’s used, and who can see it.
privacy.accountText: your university email address (@andrew.ac.jp) and display name
privacy.membershipText: the classes and teams you join
privacy.contentText: your team project’s tasks and the progress you log (including any memo on a log), check-ins, your answers to meeting polls, nudges, and text you write with Write in Study Pods, with its history
privacy.googleText: the character count or number of slides of the files you choose (or of the Doc created for your group), when it was checked, and an encrypted connection token
privacy.notifyText: your device’s push address (an address and encryption keys issued by your browser), your display language and the kind of device (e.g. Safari on iPhone), so we can deliver them. Notifications are off until you turn them on, and you can turn them off in 設定 at any time. Turning them off or logging out deletes that device’s address.
privacy.cookieText: only to keep you logged in, remember your language, and remember two small display settings (whether you’ve chosen a display name, and whether you’ve seen the setup-complete message). No advertising or analytics cookies. Whether you’ve closed the notification suggestion is saved only in this device’s browser, not in a cookie.
privacy.noText: With Write in Study Pods, we store the text you write and its history (up to the latest 50 versions). Only you can read it. Teammates see only its character count, never the text. Teachers see neither the text nor your own character count. Otherwise we never store the text of your reports or assignments. Text that hasn’t been saved yet is kept for a short time in this device’s browser so a lost connection doesn’t lose it. It is deleted when you log out, when the login page is next opened on this device, or after 7 days.
privacy.useText: Only to run the service (sharing progress with your team, nudges and similar features) and for the research use in section 6. We don’t use your data for advertising, and we don’t sell it.
privacy.googleIntro: Google Docs and Google Slides data is handled as follows.
privacy.google1: Connecting Google is optional. If you do, the service can open only the files you select in Google’s file picker and the Doc it creates for your group (the drive.file permission). It cannot read the rest of your Google Drive.
privacy.google2: A file’s text is read only to count its characters or slides, and is never stored, logged or shared. Only the count and when it was checked are saved. Teammates see only that number; nobody sees the text.
privacy.google3: Connection tokens are stored encrypted and used on our server only. A group Doc created by the service is set to “anyone with the link can edit” (or, when a university Google account doesn’t allow that, anyone at the university with the link), and that link is shown only to your team’s members.
privacy.google4: You can disconnect Google at any time in Settings. We then revoke the permission at Google and delete the stored token.
privacy.limitedUse: Study Pods’ use and transfer of information received from Google APIs to any other app will adhere to the <link>Google API Services User Data Policy</link>, including the Limited Use requirements.
privacy.podText: your display name, the tasks you own and their numbers (visible as soon as you log), your check-ins, your answers to meeting polls, and your nudges. Not the memos on your logs, and not the text you write.
privacy.classText: your display name, so they can invite you to a team. Not your progress.
privacy.devText: can access the database to run the service and fix problems. We open the text you write only if you ask us to. If fixing a problem ever needs it, we will ask you first.
privacy.serviceSupabase: Supabase: database, login and sending notifications (database in the Tokyo region)
privacy.serviceGoogle: Google: only if you connect Google
privacy.servicePush: Push services (Apple, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft): only if you turn on notifications. Notifications are delivered through your browser’s push service. They’re encrypted, so the service sees only that a message was sent to your device, and when.
privacy.servicesNote: Supabase, Vercel and Resend are US companies. The database is stored in their Tokyo region.
privacy.researchText: Study Pods is part of a university capstone project. The project report uses only aggregated usage figures that can’t identify you, such as how often progress is logged or how many people keep using the app. It never includes names, email addresses, the text of memos or comments, or text you write in Study Pods; for your writing, only character counts are used. If you don’t want your data included, email us at the address below and we’ll leave it out of the analysis; you can keep using the app. Whether you use Study Pods, and whether you opt out, has no effect on your grades.
privacy.retentionText: We keep your data while you use your account. Deleting a task or your account deletes the text written there and its history right away; backup copies are gone within 30 days. You can delete your account and its data at any time in 設定 → Delete account; it’s removed from our database immediately. You can also email us at the address below. Any copies, including backups, are gone within 30 days. Accounts with no login for one year are deleted. If the service shuts down, all data is deleted within 30 days. Logs kept by our hosting providers follow their own retention periods.
privacy.changesText: If this policy changes, we’ll update the effective date on this page.
privacy.priceText: Study Pods is currently free. If paid features are ever introduced, we’ll tell you in advance.
privacy.organizerLabel: Whoever created the class (e.g. a teacher):
privacy.organizerText: How many students have joined and the join link, the class project, a summary for each team (team size, overall project progress in %, whether it is on track, the day of the last activity, and how many checked in this round), and, to organize the teams, students’ display names and which team each is in. The teacher can make and name teams, move a student to another team or out of one, and post announcements to the whole class. They can’t see anyone’s individual numbers, memos, writing or email address.
privacy.teamCodeText: a team’s code and QR code are shown only to that team’s members. Anyone who has the code can join that team (and, if they aren’t in the class yet, the class as a student). Any member can make a new code at any time, and the old one stops working.
privacy.presenceLabel: When you open the app, and the online dot:
privacy.presenceText: While the app is open, we record once a minute when you last opened it. Teammates see only the day you last opened it (not the time) and whether you have it open right now (a green dot). You can turn the green dot off in Settings under “Show when I’m online”. Teachers and other classmates can’t see this, and it isn’t used for research.

google.connectTitle: Connect Google and your progress logs itself
google.connectWhy: Every 5 minutes we count the characters in your Google Docs and the slides in your Slides, and log the change. The text is never saved, and your group never sees it.
google.connectFine: You only connect once. If your university account won’t connect, your personal Google account works too.
google.groupDocWhy: Write under your own heading and your characters are logged automatically. Anyone with the link (or anyone at the university with it) can edit, so don’t share it outside your team.
google.groupDocCreateWhy: We make one Doc with a heading for each task counted in characters, and link each task to its heading. The link is shown only to this team’s members.

result.failed: Google couldn’t be connected. Please try again.
result.unavailable: Google can’t be connected right now. Please try again later.

google.linkNotCountable: This task is measured by status only, so it can’t be linked to a file.
google.lostExplain: The current file can’t be read anymore. Whoever linked it may have disconnected Google, or the file was deleted. Please link it again.

section.title: A heading in the group Doc
section.hint: Characters under the heading you choose

doc.title: My own Doc
doc.hint: Characters in the whole Doc you choose in Google’s file picker

slides.title: Google Slides
slides.hint: Number of slides in the file you choose

google.headingHint: Renaming the heading won’t break the link.
google.pickAndLink: Choose a file and link it
google.relinkNote: Relinking never counts the same work twice.
google.settingsConnectedHint: Disconnecting deletes the stored connection token. Files you linked won’t be counted until someone links them again.
google.settingsNotConnectedHint: You can link Google Docs and Slides from a project’s page.
google.noCountedTask: Add a task measured by count or characters, and it can be logged automatically from a Google file.
google.noCharactersTask: The group Doc is for tasks counted in characters. A count task can be linked to Google Slides from the task itself.

teacher.title: How the teams are doing
teacher.privacy: No student names, individual numbers or text are shown.

teamJoin.title: A team in {className}
teamJoin.body: Joining opens your team’s project board. Team numbers are visible to every member.
teamJoin.full: This team already has 6 members, so it’s full.
teamJoin.alsoJoinsClass: You’re not in this class yet, so you’ll join it as a student too.
teamJoin.invalidBody: The code may be mistyped, or the team may have made a new one. Ask your team to show you their current QR code or code.

teamInvite.heading: Invite to your team
teamInvite.body: Send the link on LINE or another app, or show this screen in class so classmates can scan the QR code. They can also type the code.
teamInvite.qrLabel: QR code to join the team ({url})
teamInvite.renew: Make a new code (the current code and QR stop working)
teamInvite.message: Join my team for {className}! Use this link: {url}
teamInvite.messageProject: Join my team for “{project}” in {className}! Use this link: {url}
teamInvite.smallTeam: Your team is still small. Invite classmates to join.

teamCodeForm.label: Join with a team code
teamCodeForm.hint: The 8-character code your team showed you. You can also scan their QR code.

classProject.title: Class project
classProject.why: Every new team in this class starts with this project and its tasks.
classProject.noTasks: No tasks yet. Pick a template or add a task.
classProject.appliesToNew: Changes apply to teams started from now on. Existing teams keep their project.

teamTable.heading: Your team
teamTable.note: “Last seen” is the day someone last opened the app, never the time. You can turn off showing you online in Settings.

organizer.heading: Manage teams
organizer.why: {students} students, {teams} teams. You see names and teams only, never progress or writing.
organizer.autoSplitLabel: Split the rest into teams automatically
organizer.announceHint: Shown on every student’s board in this class (up to {max} characters).
